text:
sam: ran a focused nsys trace on the small-seq pathways after the SLA alert. seeing big spikes from compilation tasks gated in the serving process — 80-250ms on cold shapes. attaching excerpts below.

maya: ugh. this matches the p99s we saw in Canary this morning. is this compile on-demand (jit) or triton JIT warm path?

sam: looks like Triton JIT style compile triggered per-shape. nsys timeline shows long host-side CPU time waiting in the compile executor before kernels even start. also a churn in kernel-cache lookups right before.

diego: can you paste the timeline snippet? even a tiny ascii snippet helps.

sam: sure — exported the relevant slice:
```
Timeline (nsys) slice:
0.0ms  request receive
1.2ms  queue/batching
5.6ms  compile_spawn (python)  <-- 120ms
125.6ms kernel_launch (matmul)
126.0ms kernel_exec  (matmul)
126.4ms copy_back
```
Noting: compile_spawn blocks the worker for ~120ms on first use of that shape. After that subsequent requests use cached kcache and compile is ~4-6ms.

anya: do we have metrics on compile concurrency? maybe many requests try to compile same shape at once causing thundering.

sam: yes — trace shows 6 compile tasks started for same shape over 1s window in one host. compile queue length spikes.

perf-bot: captured summary from nvprof-like sampling:
- total_compile_time: 1.1s (across 10 requests)
- avg_kernel_time_post_compile: 2.4ms
- cache_lookup_latency_p50: 0.9ms, p99: 15ms (eviction thrash)

maya: hypotheses: (1) compile tasks are single-threaded and sync, blocking request worker; (2) cache eviction TTL too short for churned shapes; (3) batching heuristics let tiny batches through which expose first-request latency.

diego: mitigation ideas:
- serialize compile per-shape (single flight) to prevent duplicate compiles.
- offload compile to a separate pool so request path isn't blocked.
- precompile top-k shapes seen from traffic (background warmers).
- extend kcache TTL and increase cache size for recent shapes.

sam: added: also consider fast-path stub kernels for common small sizes to avoid compile. and backoff / delay accepting new requests for a hot shape until compile finishes (graceful 503 or queue to other replica).

anya: good. do we have a simple repro to run locally that triggers thundering?

sam: yes, minimal harness: send 50 concurrent requests for seq_len=8 with different random prompts — most requests map to ~12 distinct shapes. I can push a reproducer in eng-runtime repro repo.

maya: action items:
- sam: upload nsys full trace + repro harness (today)
- diego: prototype compile worker pool & singleflight per-shape (next week)
- anya: change kcache TTL from 30s -> 120s and monitor memory impact (today)
- infra-bot: add canary rule to alert if compile_time_p99 > 50ms for small-seq route

infra-bot: noted. added alert: infra/alerts/compile-p99-smallseq -> triggered when p99_compile_time > 0.05s over 5m.

diego: for the worker pool approach, prefer a bounded async pool so we don't OOM; also instrument queue waiting time. I'll draft a design doc.

maya: follow-up question: are we sure kernel-cache eviction is contributing? sample trace shows cache-miss churn but need memory profile.

sam: I'll attach nvtx markers next trace and capture the kernel cache size timeline. preliminary heap snapshot shows kcache entries flapping with LRU eviction every ~40s under high variance traffic.

anya: let's sync tomorrow 11am PT to review traces and pick which mitigation to ship first (kcache TTL bump vs singleflight).

sam: thanks — I'll paste links in here when uploaded. :thumbsup:
